messages:
alex: Quick sync request — we need a concrete contract from runtime/infra for the per-model/route SLO panels we want in Console v3. Specifically: P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT, and tokens/sec by model_id + route + model_version. Who can own the emission shape?
kevin: I can take point on runtime-side emission. question: do you need raw traces or pre-aggregated rollups?
sara: console would prefer pre-aggregated minutes for dashboards to keep query cost down. we still want raw samples for debug traces but not for every request.
maya: agree with sara. also need to limit cardinality — model_version + route + region should be enough. avoid including instance_id or GPU host in the rollups.
matt: runtime can emit both histograms for latency and counters for tokens/requests. histograms: t-digest or HDR? which does Console prefer for P99 accuracy? :thinking_face:
console-ux: HDR works well for percentiles in dashboards, t-digest is smaller but can drift on extreme tails. console panels expect stable P99 across rollouts. HDR recommended.
kevin: ok we can export HDR histograms (base: 1ms, max: 60s) per (model_id, route, model_version, region) aggregated at 1m. tokens/sec: two counters (tokens, requests) and we compute rate in Grafana. TTFT: we can emit a percentile summary or a separate histogram. prefer separate histogram for TTFT to avoid mixing latencies.
alex: timeline? we need ingest contract by EOW. Also, sampling rate for raw traces?
maya: propose 0.5% default for raw traces, 100% for rollups. that keeps storage manageable while preserving debugability.
kevin: implementation note — runtime will buffer histograms and push to metrics pipeline. format (proto/json):
```
metric_name: redwood.runtime.latency_histogram
labels: {model_id, route, model_version, region, gpu_tier}
aggregation_window: 60s
histogram: HDR_base64_blob
```
we'll include a schema link in the PR.
sara: on ingest side (metrics-ingest) we need the label whitelist. @matt can you add gpu_tier to the whitelist? ops/security reqs say region must be low-cardinality.
matt: yes, will add gpu_tier (n1, v100-32g, a100-80g) and enforce label cardinality limits. also adding a metric tag indicating rollout id so Console can filter by canary vs prod.
alex: good call on rollout tag. We need a dashboard grouping toggle: group by model_version (default off) and by rollout_id (default on -> show canaries).
console-ux: UI note — grouping by model_version increases series count. we'll implement an aggregation knob: "collapse versions" which sums across versions but lets you drill down.
maya: ingestion sampling math — if customers enable dedicated capacity we might increase raw trace sampling to 2% since infra cost is contained. add that to schema as an opt-in field.
kevin: action items: 1) runtime: post PR with emission schema + example payload (kevin) 2) metrics-ingest: whitelist labels + enforce cardinality + add rollout_id tag (matt) 3) console: draft panel layouts + aggregation knob (sara & console-ux) 4) infra/platform: doc sampling defaults + opt-ins (maya). target: PRs by Thu EOD, dashboard mock by Fri.
alex: perfect. one more: include tokens/sec denominator semantics — is it tokens/request or tokens/second computed from sliding window? we want tokens/sec (throughput) in rolling 1m windows.
matt: tokens counter + requests counter per minute will make tokens/sec reliable. store as monotonic counters.
kevin: note about emergency fallback routing: when a model falls back to a smaller quantized variant we still emit rollups under the original model_id but add label fallback_variant=true so Console can surface regressions.
sara: thanks — we'll add a panel that highlights any P95 regression > 20% when fallback_variant=true.
alex: ok everyone, thanks. I'll follow up with the design doc link and the EOW checklist. :thumbsup:
ingest-bot: metric schema PR created: https://git.redwood/internal/metrics/1234 (draft) :robot_face:
kevin: saw the PR, will add example payload and HDR encoding notes today.
sara: I'll start the dashboard mock in Figma and share a link in this thread when ready.
maya: locking this in — will update sampling defaults doc and post an RFC for opt-in increases.
alex: awesome. meeting not needed unless blockers surface. ping here with any issues. :wave:
